title: Why Time Disappears As You Get Older
description:
A year at age five is twenty percent of your entire life. A year at fifty is two percent. But that is only half the answer. Here is what actually happens to your perception of time.

Made with AI assistance.

#psychology #time #brain #science #facts

scenes.narration: When you were five, a single year was twenty percent of your entire existence. Summer lasted forever. Now a year vanishes before you finish describing it.
The obvious answer is proportion. A year at fifty is just two percent of your life, so of course it feels smaller. That explanation is real, but it is only half of it.
The second half is novelty. Your brain does not record time evenly. It records change. New experiences get written down in detail. Repeats get compressed into nothing.
Think about the last trip you took. The first day feels long because almost everything was new. The ride home feels like it took minutes, because your brain skipped it.
This is why childhood was so dense. Everything was a first. Your first bicycle, your first snow, your first argument. Your brain had a reason to keep all of it.
So time does not actually speed up. You just stopped giving it anything worth remembering. Do something unfamiliar this week and watch the week get longer.
